rows.notes: aextract_data issues exactly ONE GET to a URL built by utils/url_generator.py generate_url (lines 19-96): country/date selection is NOT a second request, it is encoded as PATH SEGMENTS of the single request, e.g. /calendar/country/{country}/{start_date}/{end_date}?c= (line 55) and /calendar/country/{country}/group/{group}/{start}/{end} (line 66); bare /calendar?c= is the no-filter snapshot (line 30). generate_url branches over ~12 mutually exclusive parameter combinations via check_args (lines 49-94); missing half of a date pair is auto-filled (lines 33-36); unmatched combos return '' and the fetcher raises OpenBBError (model lines 252-255). api_key is appended to a literal ?c= suffix carried in the generated path. importance low/medium/high is mapped to 1/2/3 query numbers (model lines 121-126) and response Importance 1/2/3 back to strings (lines 180-185); payload keys arrive Capitalized and are remapped per __alias_dict__ (lines 132-155). Response is a top-level JSON array of event dicts (response_callback in utils/helpers.py lines 19-24), each dict one row; no pagination loop. endpoints=1 because one call hits exactly one path template though the template set spans ~12 paths. C93 added the four mechanisms this row used to leave unrecorded: generate_url fills a missing half of the date pair at :33-36 -- end_date becomes date.today().strftime('%Y-%m-%d') (:34) and start_date becomes a copy of end_date (:35-36) -- both recorded under relative_date_default (param.relative_default) because one carrier refuses both, ParamSpec.default holding a literal; the two halves are different rules and are named here so the fold stays visible (#86's shape). Response side the Data model maps the published Importance integer back to a word with value_to_string = {1: Low, 2: Medium, 3: High} at :180-185, which is code_table_reverse_lookup (columns.compose) rather than the request-side param_value_mapping this row already carried, and clears empty strings to None at :206-217 (sentinel_value_nulling); date, last_updated and reference_date are parsed through to_datetime with microseconds zeroed and reference_date truncated to a date (:187-204), which is date_format (columns.cast). The importance map is genuinely two-directional: :121-126 sends the word as a number and :180-185 reads the number back as a word, and only the second half is response-side.
